methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Kraftblock is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Martin Schichtel and Susanne König, having raised €20M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company (LNZA) operating in the climate and energy sector, including later-stage companies such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The peer-median method anchors the analysis. Three same-sector comparables at Series C or adjacent stage—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—yield a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B. This method is applicable given the availability of recent financings in the same sector and development stage.

The triangulation across available methods supports a valuation range of $850M to $1.1B, with a median point estimate of $1.0B. The analysis relies on a single quantitative method, reflecting data constraints; the range reflects both the peer sample spread and stage-adjusted positioning within the comparable set. Key uncertainties include the timing and quantum of Series B fundraising relative to the peer benchmarks, technology differentiation relative to Electric Hydrogen and Amogy, and capital intensity of the underlying business model. Additional triangulation methods would require proprietary financial data not presently available.
